edits.replacement:
Issue 521 addresses the mismatch between the FLOW_COMMANDS parser contract and displayed help. The authoritative 2026-09-24 restart contract supersedes the historical audit counts and unresolved revision 008. It requires current-registry re-enumeration, a shared structured option model, reuse of existing owners, preservation of rejection lifecycle and runtime paths, and a per-leaf inventory and owner map.

Source verification found that src/flow/registry.js owns FLOW_COMMANDS leaf args, help, lazy handlers, lifecycle hooks, target metadata, and runtime metadata; src/lib/command-registry.js projects those entries into CommandDefinition and currently reverse-parses hand-written help; src/lib/dispatcher.js owns splitArgsBySpec, parseEntryInput, cli.parseArgs, implicit -h/--help, required and optional values, equals syntax, positional/rest handling, and unknown/missing/extra input boundaries; and src/help.js has a second fixed-width subcommand renderer. The Spec therefore makes the registry-bound structured option model the authority for parser, Usage, Options, leaf help, and direct-child group help, while retaining command prose, examples, and locale text.

The current checkout enumerates 68 FLOW_COMMANDS leaves: query, resume, prepare, get 11, set 17, run 36, and report/show 1. The 67 routed leaves exclude query. Query remains the independent bootstrapFlowQueryCli contract owned by src/flow/query.js and src/flow/query-contract.js, including stdin, --request-file, bounded request/response, cursor, schema, help, and error behavior. Current inventory and tests must derive their denominator and group intersections from the registry rather than hard-code historical 66, 65, 67, or 34/36 counts.

The structured model uses dedicated option and command-row classes with constructor invariants. An option records canonical name, aliases, flag/required-value/optional-value kind, placeholder, and description. A row records name, summary, optional display order, and full path. Implicit -h, --help is one explicit option row. Group options are the full option-contract intersection of every direct child leaf, including aliases and value kind; therefore --agent-work-dir belongs to run and not get, set, or report/show. Canonical name order is locale-independent, with explicit display order lower-first, absent-last, and name as the tie-breaker. Rows use at least two ASCII spaces between name and summary, including the 13/14/15 character boundary, recover-missing-producer-artifact, and renderer-only synthetic 64/65 character names; synthetic names do not create a production command-name limit.

The per-leaf inventory distinguishes parser syntax from domain validation. Positionals, rest, flags, required-value options, optional-value options, and implicit help are enumerated from the registry. FlowSpecId, PreparingFlowId, FlowTargetExpectation, target binding, canonical file map, review evidence, task-review host filtering, and each command handler retain ownership of format, domain, conditional combinations, path roots, and existing limits. Internal _rawArgs, resolved targets, injected runtime state, and runtime-log metadata are not public options. Existing explicit limits remain owner contracts; an absent limit remains absent, and help consistency does not authorize a universal validator or arbitrary resource policy.

Verification uses registry traversal plus real dispatcher/CLI behavior for leaf help, all three group-help routes, parser acceptance, guard matches and mismatches, runtime paths, rejection order, lifecycle hooks, diagnostics, and exit codes. It assigns hook, configuration, generated-artifact, side-effect, and query checks to their existing owners and behavior-level tests. The bounded test contract is explicit: the contract traversal fails closed above 8 nested registry levels, 256 routed leaves, or 1 MiB of canonical inventory/help input. These are test-harness safety bounds and review triggers, not new production command limits; the current three-level routed tree and 67 routed leaves are within them.

The bounded-resource-usage exception is intentional only for the registry/help contract: recursive traversal, retries, and bulk input are never unbounded in the test harness, and existing retry and bulk-data limits remain owned by their current modules. A bound or retry policy change is outside this help-contract scope and requires a separate reviewed change.

The value contract is owned by the named command or value class, not inferred from a shared spelling. `--spec` on resume is a FlowSpecId: a non-empty literal matching [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*, with no double dot and no trailing dot or .lock; `--spec` on run gate is an existing file path resolved by run-gate against its execution root, and it may be relative or absolute only as that owner permits. `--spec-id` is the same FlowSpecId and must be paired with --version; --version is a positive safe integer. `--base` on prepare and lint is a Git branch name resolved by the existing Git owner. `--issue` is a positive integer and is validated by prepare or set-init/set-issue owners. `--title`, --request, --text, --message, --answer, --why, --considered, --dropped-reason, --search, --notes, --record-evidence, --remaining-risk, and free-form --reason values are UTF-8 strings with non-empty trimmed content where their owner requires a value; there is no new universal text maximum.

The five shared target guards are owned by FlowTargetExpectation and FlowTargetBinding in src/lib/flow-target-guard.js. --expect-no-issue is a valueless boolean and conflicts with --expect-issue. --expect-issue is a positive safe integer. --expect-spec is a FlowSpecId. --expect-run-id is a non-empty trimmed target token of at most 300 characters; it is not a generic 100-character ID. --expect-binding is a base64url serialized version-2 binding, at most 32 KiB, and cannot be combined with conflicting explicit target fields. A matching guard selects the same run/spec/Issue/authority; a mismatch is rejected before command-owned mutation. Missing guards retain each command's existing behavior.

--run-id has owner-specific meanings. On prepare it selects a PreparingFlowId with the existing safe identifier grammar and 200-character maximum. On set request, set note, set auto, and auto-check it selects the preparing-flow owner with that same rule. On get status it is the optional positional selector. On get runtime-log it is runId or runId#sequence, where sequence is a positive decimal integer; an explicit --sequence must match the suffix. Other occurrences of --expect-run-id are target guards, not PreparingFlowIds. --task-id is an existing canonical task identifier resolved by the active Flow; --normalized-finding-id is an existing issue-log finding identifier; neither gets a new global regex or length rule.

Other domains are explicit: get check target is dirty, gh, impl, or finalize; get prompt kind is a prompt-registry key; get artifact logicalKey is spec.record or acceptance.review; get guardrail phase is VALID_GUARDRAIL_PHASES with impl mapped to task-impl and --format is json or default Markdown; get runtime-log --format accepts only json and --sequence is positive decimal. set step id is an existing step identifier and status is VALID_STEP_STATUSES. set draft-answer questionId must be the selected Draft question, question-revision is a non-negative safe integer, and --drop is mutually exclusive with answer/why/considered while dropped-reason requires --drop. set broad action is on and --step is implement, impl-review, or impl-gate. set policy value is nonblocking. set nonblocking-decision --choice is repair, retry, or continue; reason is non-empty and continue requires non-empty --remaining-risk; --expect-evidence-digest is a lowercase SHA-256 digest. set metric phase and counter are VALID_PHASES and VALID_METRIC_COUNTERS. set approval requires --approved, --confirmed-at is ISO 8601, and --notes is at most 2000 characters. set acceptance-decision --choice is accept_risk_and_continue or abort. set auto value is on or off.

set issue-log requires --step and a trimmed --reason of at least 20 characters. trigger, resolution, and guardrail-candidate, when present, are trimmed strings of at least 10 characters. --repair-ref-commit is 7 to 40 hexadecimal characters; --repair-ref-file is a non-empty path; --task-id must exist in the current task set. set retry action is reset, kind is gate or review, phase is respectively gate phases task-impl or integration, or review phases draft, draft-questions, draft-coverage, spec, test, or impl; --yes and --reason are required by the existing RetryRecovery owner.

Run-specific values retain their owners. --approve is the exact non-empty dispatcher approval token. --phase on recover-review-pass is draft-questions, draft-coverage, spec, test, or impl; on review it is a VALID_REVIEW_PHASES value; on gate it is a VALID_GATE_PHASES value. reopen-draft --category is task-addition or spec-correction, with spec-correction requiring its existing target guards and reason. reconcile-task-review --dry-run previews, --yes requires the exact --expect-digest, and --reason is 20 to 500 characters. filter-task-review --exclusions is a JSON array whose entries have exactly non-empty findingId and reason; the host filter permits at most 256 findings and rejects unknown or duplicate IDs. Its four expect values are lineage inputs owned by that command: attempt ID is non-empty, and review/source/catalog fingerprints are SHA-256 digests. --task-id, --json, --base, and final-regression values are validated by their run-* owners. --json for update-overview is an object with modules, data_flow, and decisions arrays; each entry is at most 500 characters. --record-category is an existing final-regression category: existing, environment, sandbox, timeout, dependency, out_of_scope, or flaky_suspected; --record-evidence and --remaining-risk are required for explicit out_of_scope or flaky_suspected recording.

Path contracts remain owner-specific. --agent-work-dir is a file-system path resolved by the existing root/config resolver; invocation override has priority over config.agent.workDir and .tmp, while config.logs.dir controls logDir when present and otherwise logs are under agentWorkDir/logs. Both slash and equals option forms must feed the same resolver; finalize-cleanup retains its durable-root policy. run gate --spec is a file path and must exist when supplied. set review-evidence --file must be an existing bounded regular JSON file inside the active spec directory; its existing review-evidence limit is 1 MiB. get context path is an analysis/file path resolved by get-context; with no path it is list mode, and --search is keyword text. set files paths are one or more normalized repository-relative paths owned by CanonicalFileMap; reqId must be a requirement id. Do not require output directories to exist before the owner creates them.

Existing resource policies are recorded without adding new ones: review evidence is bounded to 1 MiB; Task Review exclusions are bounded to 256 entries; update-overview entries are bounded to 500 characters; approval notes are bounded to 2000 characters; nonblocking reason and remaining-risk strings are bounded to 2000 characters; review subprocess retry count and delay remain the existing run-review owner values of 2 and 30 seconds. The set-files command has no additional CLI count or aggregate-size rule beyond CanonicalFileMap and its Store. get-context keeps its existing analysis/prompt traversal and read policies; this Spec adds no replacement depth, count, or read-size rule. Query request-file size, collection, and depth bounds remain only in src/flow/query-contract.js and are regression-tested separately. No retry, attempt, path, text, or JSON policy is copied into a new common validator.

The shared registry option model projects parser args, leaf help, and group help, and the direct-child intersection compares full option contracts including aliases and value kind. Contract tests use the inventory to cover every routed leaf, required-value space and equals syntax, optional positional/rest cardinality, owner validation, implicit help, and the query exclusion. Focused real CLI tests cover all three group-help entry points, group intersections, ordering and spacing, guard match/mismatch, runtime-path forms, exit status, and one behavior-level assertion for each retained public surface. Existing command modules, validators, hooks, configuration, generated artifacts, side effects, and lifecycle transitions remain the owners of execution behavior.

edits.replacement:
The help projection change must not change execution responsibility, validation, guard evaluation, lifecycle, diagnostics, or exit-code behavior. This contract applies to every current routed leaf: resume; prepare; get status, resolve-context, check, prompt, artifact, qa-count, guardrail, issue, next-action, context, and runtime-log; set step, request, issue, note, draft-answer, files, review-evidence, broad, policy, nonblocking-decision, metric, approval, issue-log, init, retry, acceptance-decision, and auto; run seal-handoff, dispatch, recover-review-pass, gate, review, auto-check, finalize-commit, finalize-merge, finalize-sync, finalize-cleanup, abort, sync, reopen-draft, repair-plan-gate, settle-failure, settle-review-transition, recover-missing-producer-artifact, recover-spec-gate-repair, recover-draft-execution, reconcile-task-review, filter-task-review, recover-finalization, recover-task-execution-overrun, claim-next-action, settle-gate-transition, start-task, complete-task, update-overview, lint, test-execute, requirement-test-gate, test-result-review, retro, final-regression, acceptance-review, and report; and report/show. The list is regenerated from FLOW_COMMANDS, not used as a hard-coded denominator.

For each listed leaf, a valid invocation means that its declared positional/rest cardinality, parser syntax, existing owner validation, and any applicable target guard are satisfied; it returns process exit code 0 and performs only its documented command behavior. Explicit -h or --help is valid, prints the leaf help, returns 0, and does not execute the handler, lifecycle hook, runtime log operation, or mutation. A group with no leaf prints group help but returns 1, while an unknown group or leaf, missing required value, unknown option, extra positional, invalid owner value, target mismatch, or command/lifecycle failure returns 1. Query is outside this shared contract and keeps its independent query exit and error behavior.

Preserve parseEntryInput and cli.parseArgs required-value and optional-value rules, --name=value, missing/unknown/extra input, and P/rest behavior. Preserve FlowTargetExpectation and FlowTargetBinding matching, mismatch, mutual exclusion, and identity checks before command-owned mutation. Preserve the existing pre, post, onError, and finally ordering, envelope diagnostics, and runtime log behavior, including the current fact that parse failures may resolve context or open a log. Both --agent-work-dir /path and --agent-work-dir=/path must reach the same existing resolver: invocation override, then configured agent.workDir, then .tmp; config.logs.dir controls logDir when set, otherwise it is agentWorkDir/logs, and finalize-cleanup retains its durable-root policy. Valid help must never run execution hooks.

The implementation and tests must not introduce a new blanket validator, arbitrary resource limit, target-guard decision, query migration, or command semantic change. Registry/parser contract tests cover every routed leaf and focused real dispatcher/CLI tests cover valid help, representative valid execution, guard match and mismatch, runtime path forms, abort/get/set/run behavior, group intersection and no-leaf exit status.

Derive leaf counts and direct-child group intersections at test time; keep flow query as the independent parser/help exception. Contract-side recursion is bounded to 8 registry levels, 256 routed leaves, and 1 MiB of canonical inventory/help input, with overflow failing closed and requiring a reviewed scope update. These are test-harness bounds only: they do not add a production resource policy or change command semantics, validators, target guards, runtime paths, lifecycle, or query behavior.

finding.body:
**Target:** R1/R3 and T1-T3
**Issue:** FLOW_COMMANDS.args contains option token names, while placeholders and descriptions currently exist only in raw help text parsed by command-registry.flowOptions(). The spec forbids help reverse-parsing but does not identify where the required CommandOption description, placeholder, alias, kind, and row summary values come from.
**Required change:** Specify the concrete FLOW_COMMANDS or CommandDefinition field/factory that owns structured option and summary metadata, including common guard/runtime options, and state that raw help remains prose rather than an authority.
**Why blocking:** Without that source, implementation must either retain the forbidden reverse parser or create an undocumented parallel authority, and tests have no stable expected display contract.
finding.evidence: The immutable spec bans help reverse-parsing and requires structured option metadata, but does not identify the concrete FLOW_COMMANDS or CommandDefinition field/factory that owns those values; the authority must be named in the requirement text.

finding.body:
**Target:** R3/T3: routed leaf --help
**Issue:** The current dispatcher returns entry.help directly when help is requested; flow.js uses that dispatcher path for leaf help. CommandDefinition.renderHelp() only renders group subcommands, and the spec does not identify the integration point that replaces the raw leaf help with projected Usage/Options rows.
**Required change:** Name the routed leaf integration point—such as the dispatcher help shortcut calling a shared leaf renderer—and define how raw prose, locale data, and projected options are combined.
**Why blocking:** Updating only CommandDefinition/group rendering leaves commands such as flow run abort --help on the old raw help, so parser/help parity is not achieved.

finding.body:
**Target:** R7 and src/lib/command-registry.js query projection
**Issue:** FLOW_COMMANDS.query is currently included in flowSubcommands, coreCommandRegistry metadata, routePaths/helpPaths, and the public sennel help flow query route. R7 says query must not appear in CommandDefinition projection but provides no replacement for that existing help/catalog behavior.
**Required change:** State that query is excluded only from routed option/group/inventory projections while its independent CommandDefinition metadata route remains, or specify and test a replacement owner for sennel help flow query and catalog listing.
**Why blocking:** Literal removal from CommandDefinition changes an existing public help route, while query integration tests do not cover that regression.

finding.body:
**Target:** R1/R4/T4-T5; src/lib/namespace-dispatcher.js and src/help.js
**Issue:** CommandDefinition.renderHelp() is also used by NamespaceDispatcher for docs, check, metrics, spec, and hook namespaces, while CommandDefinition.metadata()/help rendering serves all core and plugin help. The spec does not define an opt-in boundary for the new Flow-specific structured renderer or preservation of these non-flow surfaces.
**Required change:** Explicitly scope the new projection/renderer to routed Flow definitions and preserve existing non-flow NamespaceDispatcher/help behavior, or include those consumers and their regressions in scope.
**Why blocking:** A global CommandDefinition change can alter or break unrelated namespace help while the proposed Flow-focused tests would not detect it.
